title: Enchilada Sauce
description: DaVita dietitians, Kara and Maria from Arizona, have put together a regional menu of favorite foods from the Southwest. This dialysis-friendly recipe for Enchilada Sauce features the ingredients that are plentiful in the American Southwest.
steps: Drain tomatoes.
Heat oil in skillet. Stir in diced tomatoes, garlic powder, 1 teaspoon chili powder and salt.
In a small cup, mix together cornstarch with 1/2 cup water. Stir until smooth.
Add the cornstarch mixture to hot tomatoes while stirring to blend well.
Reduce heat and simmer until thickened.
Taste and add more chili powder if desired.
hints: Prepare sauce 2 to 3 days ahead and refrigerate. Use for a quick enchilada meal later in the week.
When eating a dish prepared with this sauce, count as a replacement for 1 vegetable to keep potassium in balance if you are following a low-potassium diet.
Regular canned enchilada sauces contain 150 to 400 mg sodium per 1/4 cup.

title: Egg and Sausage Breakfast Sandwich
description: For people on a kidney diet you can skip the drive-thru and still get all the flavor by making your breakfast at home. This recipe for Egg and Sausage Breakfast Sandwich by DaVita renal dietitian, Sara from California, lets you enjoy a hearty and tasty breakfast that is lower in sodium, potassium and phosphorus than what you would get at a restaurant.
ingredients: 1 tablespoon shredded natural sharp cheddar cheese
steps: In a small skillet sprayed with nonstick cooking spray, pour egg product and cook over medium low heat. When egg appears almost cooked through, turn over with a spatula and cook additional 30 seconds.
Toast English muffin.
Place turkey sausage patty on a plate, cover with a paper towel and cook in the microwave for 1 minute or the time recommended on package.
Assemble cooked egg on English muffin (fold to fit muffin). Top with sausage patty, then sharp cheddar cheese and remaining muffin half.
hints: For comparison, a fast food sausage egg sandwich contains 800 to 1,135 mg sodium, 280 mg phosphorus, 30 grams fat and 255 mg cholesterol.
Replacing egg with low-cholesterol egg product helps reduce phosphorus, cholesterol and fat.
English muffin size: 2 ounces; turkey sausage patty size: 1 ounce. Look for sausage with lowest sodium content.

title: Slow Cooker Turkey with Carrots & Cranberry Gravy
description: A delicious turkey dish shouldn’t be Thanksgiving-only fare. Slow Cooker Turkey Breast with Carrots and Cranberry Gravy was created exclusively for DaVita.com by DaVita renal dietitian, Sara from California, to provide a tasty renal-friendly recipe that’s easy to make.
serving_size: 2-1/2 ounces turkey, 1/3 cup vegetables, 1/4 cup cranberry gravy
steps: Dice the onion. Slice the celery and carrots.
Place the turkey breast in a slow cooker and sprinkle with poultry seasoning and bouillon granules.
Spoon cranberry sauce on top; add the vegetables.
Cover slow cooker with a lid, turn heat to high and cook for 4 hours.
Remove turkey breast and slice. Serve with vegetables and cranberry gravy.
hints: Whole turkey breast may be substituted for boneless turkey.
Spray slow cooker pot with nonstick cooking spray or use a slow cooker liner for easier cleanup.
Frozen onion and carrots may be used instead of fresh vegetables.
A very small portion of regular bouillon adds flavor. Portion control helps keep sodium content within the limits of a low-sodium diet.
Serve with noodles, rolls, margarine and fruit salad.

title: Make Ahead Pancake or Waffle Batter for a Crowd
description: DaVita dietitian Mary shares her kidney-friendly take on this breakfast time batter, Make Ahead Pancake or Waffle Batter for a Crowd. The fun thing about this recipe is you can please everyone, from the pancake lover to the waffle fanatic.
serving_size: one 4" pancake or half of a 4" x 4" waffle
steps: Lightly spoon flour into measuring cup and level off.
In a large bowl, combine flour, sugar, salt and yeast.
In a medium saucepan, heat milk and butter until warmed to 120-140°F.
Add warm liquid and eggs to flour mixture and beat with a mixer at medium speed until smooth.
Cover and refrigerate at least 1 hour or up to 4 days, adding 2 tablespoons sugar after the second day.
For pancakes, lightly grease a griddle or skillet, heat and pour 1/4 cup batter for each pancake. Turn pancakes when edges look dry and bubbles begin to break on the surface.
For waffles, bake 1/2 cup batter in a hot waffle iron until steaming stops.
hints: The yeast in this recipe replaces baking powder, a high phosphorus, high sodium ingredient.

title: Festive Egg Scramble
description: Colorful bell peppers make this kidney-friendly Festive Egg Scramble recipe special for any morning.
ingredients: 3-1/2 cups liquid low cholesterol egg substitute
steps: Finely chop onion and bell peppers.
Combine egg product, onion, bell peppers and black pepper in a bowl.
Melt margarine in a skillet. Add egg mixture and cook until eggs are set. Stir often to prevent sticking.
Serve hot or place in warmer until ready to serve.
hints: Low cholesterol egg substitute is available refrigerated or frozen. Best choices for kidney patients are brands lowest in sodium without added soy or milk products or phosphate additives.

title: Lemon-Rosemary Barbeque Chicken
description: Lemon-Rosemary Barbeque Chicken may have a fancy name, and it sure has a fancy taste, but cooking and prep time are quick and easy for this kidney-friendly recipe.
ingredients: 1 pound chicken thighs, bone in, with skin
steps: Rinse chicken under cold water, pat dry with paper towel, and place chicken pieces skin-side-down in a 2-quart baking dish, Pyrex® bowl or other oven-safe cookware.
Pour oil and lemon juice into a 16-ounce container (with a tight-fitting lid) and shake to mix.
Mix black pepper, garlic powder and rosemary flakes together, reserving two teaspoons for later use. Add remaining spices to lemon/oil mixture, and shake until blended.
Sprinkle one teaspoon of the reserved spices over the chicken, cover and marinate overnight or at least 8 hours.
Pre-heat oven to 350° F. Uncover chicken and bake in oven for 25 minutes. (Leave chicken in the marinade.)
Remove from oven and turn chicken so that skin side is up. Sprinkle with remaining teaspoon of the spice mixture.
Bake for an additional 25 to 30 minutes or until chicken pieces are no longer pink inside.
Pour some of the remaining liquid over chicken when serving.
hints: Use chicken breasts or a combination of breasts and thighs if desired.
Season with garlic powder and rosemary to your personal taste. Amounts are suggestions only.
Use 1 teaspoon fresh rosemary instead of dried if available.
The longer the dish marinates the more flavorful. Marinate at least 8 hours but for full flavor, overnight.
If you are on a protein-limited diet, decrease the portion to match your meal plan.

title: Spaghetti Squash Parmigiano
description: Imagine a dish similar to pasta but without the carbs and you have DaVita renal dietitian Melissa’s Spaghetti Squash Parmigiano. It’s simple to make and can be served alone or as a pasta replacement topped with your favorite kidney-friendly pasta sauce.
steps: Preheat oven to 375º F.
Pierce spaghetti squash with a fork. Microwave for 5 minutes to soften. Cut the spaghetti squash in half and remove seeds and membranes.
Rub squash with olive oil. Place squash cut side down on a lightly greased baking sheet and bake for 50 minutes. Remove squash from oven and set aside to cool enough to be easily handled.
Finely chop garlic and shallot. Finely grate Parmigiano-Reggiano cheese.
Heat 2 tablespoons olive oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add garlic and shallot; cook and stir until fragrant, 2-3 minutes. Turn off heat.
Use a large spoon to scoop the stringy pulp from the squash into the skillet. Add Parmesan cheese, black pepper and red pepper chili flakes; stir to combine.
Remove to a serving dish and serve warm.
hints: Spaghetti squash is the only lower potassium winter squash, and is a tasty low carbohydrate substitute for pasta. It weighs from 4 to 8 pounds.
4 pound squash yields 5 cups
5 pound squash yields 6-1/4 cups
6 pound squash yields 7-1/2 cups
7 pound squash yields 8-3/4 cups
8 pound squash yields 10 cups
Heat winter squash for 4-5 minutes in the microwave for easier cutting before baking. Cool for 10 to 15 minutes before cutting.

For a lower phosphorus and sodium version, reduce the cheese to 1/2 cup. Instead of adding to the squash during preparation, sprinkle 1 tablespoon on top of each serving. Sodium is reduced to 142 mg and phosphorus is 79 mg.
Serving suggestion: Top with with Roasted Red Pepper Tomato Sauce or your favorite kidney-friendly sauce.

title: Cabbage Rolls made with Turkey
description: DaVita renal dietitian, Wendy from Ohio, shares her kidney-friendly recipe for Cabbage Rolls made with Turkey. Try this cabbage-wrapped dish and treat your family to something new.
steps: Carefully remove 12 cabbage leaves from a whole cabbage and wash them.
Boil a large pot of water. Add cabbage leaves and cook for 2 minutes to soften. Drain and set leaves aside.
In a large bowl, combine ground turkey, rice, onion, eggs, 1/4 teaspoon pepper, basil, parsley and 1/4 cup water.
Place 1/4 cup of the turkey mixture on the cabbage leaf and fold sides of leaf over turkey mixture.
Place rolls close together, seam side down in a baking dish.

Combine tomato paste, lemon juice, 1 cup water, 1/4 teaspoon pepper and sugar to make a sauce. Top cabbage rolls with sauce. Cover and bake at 375° F for 1-1/2 hour. Uncover and bake 30 minutes longer.
hints: Cabbage rolls can be cooked in a slow cooker on low setting for 6 to 8 hours instead of baked in the oven.
If you are following a low-potassium diet, be aware 2 cabbage rolls are equal to 2 vegetable servings. Consuming extra servings of fruits or vegetables can cause high potassium levels.

title: Avocado Toast with Egg
description: Make this avocado toast and egg for your breakfast or brunch. DaVita’s recipes are delicious, kidney-friendly, and submitted by DaVita dietitians.
steps: Toast the bread slices. Chop the parsley and set aside.
Remove half an avocado from the skin and mash with a fork. Combine with lime juice and salt. Spread the mixture onto each piece of toast.
Spray a skillet with cooking spray and heat over medium heat. Crack the eggs into the skillet and cook to desired doneness.
Slide eggs from the skillet onto the top of the avocado on each toast. Top each egg with 1 tablespoon feta cheese, chopped parsley and ground black pepper.
hints: Avocados are high in potassium. By limiting the amount to 1/4th of a medium avocado (approximately 1/4 cup) you can still include it on a kidney diet when potassium levels are well controlled. Ask your dietitian for individual guidance.

title: Lemony-Garlic Chicken with Quinoa and Orzo
description: DaVita renal dietitian Dara from Idaho has always had a passion for fitness and food. Dara understands that making healthy food isn’t enough, it must also be delicious. Her recipe for Lemony-Garlic Chicken with Quinoa and Orzo provides good lean protein and an exceptional lemony and garlicky flavor.
steps: Cook orzo and quinoa according to package directions and set aside.
Mince garlic; dice onion and bell pepper; slice mushrooms.
Cut chicken into 1″ pieces. Place chicken in a zippered plastic bag with juice from 1 lemon and 1 tablespoon of salt-free herb seasoning blend. Mix together and place in the refrigerator.

Heat 1/2 tablespoon olive oil in medium nonstick skillet over medium heat. Add garlic and onion. Sauté until onion is translucent (about 3 to 5 minutes). Add bell pepper and mushrooms. Cook, stirring occasionally, until peppers are just tender (about 5 to 7 minutes). Remove from heat and set aside.
Heat 1 tablespoon olive oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium heat. Add chicken and cook until no longer pink inside (about 7 minutes).
Whisk together remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil, juice of 1 lemon and 1/2 tablespoon salt-free herb seasoning blend and add to chicken.
Stir in cooked orzo, quinoa and sautéed vegetables, and then cook another 3 to 5 minutes until chicken is fully cooked and all ingredients are heated through.
Divide evenly to make 4 portions.
hints: Two ounces dry orzo pasta and two ounces dry quinoa yield 1 cup each when cooked.

title: Zucchini Bread
description: DaVita renal dietitian Eileen from California has the perfect recipe: Zucchini Bread. Not only is it kidney-friendly and tasty, the extra loaf freezes well so you can enjoy it twice as much.
ingredients: 3/4 cups sugar or Splenda® granular sweetener
steps: Preheat oven to 325° F.
Grease two 8-1/2″ x 4-1/2″ loaf pans.
In a large bowl, mix flour, sugar, pumpkin pie spice, baking soda and salt.
In medium bowl, beat eggs slightly. Stir in zucchini, honey, oil, applesauce, lemon juice and vanilla.
Stir liquid mixture into flour mixture just until flour is moistened. Spread evenly in loaf pans.
Bake 1 hour or until toothpick comes out clean.
Cool in pan on wire racks for 10 minutes, then remove from pans.
Cut each loaf into 12 slices.
hints: Boost protein content to 4 grams by adding 7 tablespoons of your favorite protein powder to dry ingredients.
If Splenda® is used instead of sugar, carbohydrate is decreased to 22 grams and 1-1/2 carbohydrate choices.
Zucchini bread freezes well. Wrap in plastic wrap, then place in a freezer bag.
If desired, use 2/3 cup applesauce and omit the oil, or use 2/3 cup oil and omit the applesauce.

title: Basic Meat Coating Mix
description: Make homemade breadcrumbs using this kidney-friendly recipe for Basic Meat Coating Mix recipe to ensure you have a low-sodium way to add flavor and crunch to beef, chicken and fish. Coat meat and fry or bake. Try adding different spices to the Basic Meat Coating Mix depending on what type of meat you use to enhance flavor.
steps: Blend ingredients in a food processor or a blender. Store until ready to use.
When ready to use, dip fresh meat into margarine or oil, then coat with coating mix, one piece at a time.
Bake meat in the oven or fry in a skillet.
hints: Make homemade dry breadcrumbs by toasting bread in the oven until dry and crisp. Process in a food processor or blender to make crumbs.
This mix keeps well in the freezer. Make extra for later use.
Try the following variations for additional flavors:
Beef or veal: add 1/2 teaspoon marjoram or oregano
Chicken: add 1/2 teaspoon thyme and ½ teaspoon sage

title: Turkey Pot Pie
description: Even if someone in your house is on a kidney diet, they can still enjoy all the baked-in goodness of this mouth-watering Turkey Pot Pie, thanks to DaVita renal dietitian Mary Beth from Louisiana.
steps: Peel and dice potatoes. Chop onionand celery. Cut cooked turkey into cubes.
Double boil potatoes to reduce potassium (see instructions in helpful hints below).
Preheat oven to 425° F.
Melt 1 tablespoon butter in large saucepan and sauté onions until tender.
Add celery and cook for an additional minute.
Blend in 2 tablespoons of flour, pepper, sage and thyme and cook over low heat for 1 minute.
Remove from heat. Stir in chicken broth and milk until blended. Bring to a boil and simmer for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Stir in turkey, double boiled potatoes and peas and carrots. Set aside to cool.
In a separate bowl, cut 1 cup of butter into remaining flour using a pastry blender. Mixture should form pea-size particles.
Begin adding ice water, one tablespoon at a time, mixing well each time, until dough forms into a ball.

Divide dough in half and roll out one piece, using a rolling pin and additional flour until dough is pliable and no longer sticky. Be sure that dough is larger than the diameter of the 9-inch pie pan.
Place dough in pie pan, smoothing with fingers to fill pan, and then pour turkey mixture on top.
Roll second piece of dough to similar size and place on top of the turkey pie filling. Seal edges of pie.
Using a sharp knife, make four to five one-inch cuts across the top of the pie crust to vent the pie.
Place pie on sheet pan and bake for 35-40 minutes or until golden brown.
hints: To reduce potassium in potatoes use the Double Cook method. Peel and dice potatoes into 1” pieces. Boil in a large pot of water for 10 minutes. Drain the water and add fresh water to the pot. Bring to a boil and cook until potatoes are tender.
Use a refrigerated, prepared pie crust if desired. Look for the lowest sodium brand.
For a lower fat and calorie version make half the pastry and use to top pie ingredients instead of the double pastry version.

title: Tabbouleh Salad
description: Tabbouleh Salad is a popular Middle Eastern dish that combines bulgur, spring onions, fresh parsley, mint, olive oil, and lemon juice. This kidney-friendly combination keeps well in the refrigerator, so make a batch to serve throughout the week.
steps: Wash bulgur. Drain and place in a large bowl. Pour 1/2 cup boiling water over bulgur, cover bowl and let sit for 30 minutes. Drain excess liquid (if any).
Dice tomato; chop peeled cucumber, green onions, parsley and mint.
Add vegetables to bulgur and mix well.
Juice the 3 lemons. Add olive oil, lemon juice, salt and pepper to bulgur mixture.
Let salad set at room temperature for about an hour to absorb the lemon juice and olive oil before serving. Refrigerate leftovers and serve during the week.
hints: Eat Tabbouleh Salad with lettuce leaves, tender grape leaves, or with a fork.
Bulgur is wheat berries that have been cracked (also known as cracked wheat). It is available in grinds from fine to extra course. Use fine or medium grind bulgur for this recipe.
One bunch of parsley, green onions or mint yields approximately 1 cup chopped.

title: Strawberry Lemon Rosemary Water
description: This drink is not only beautiful, it is refreshing. Giving plain water a flavorful twist.
steps: Hull and slice the strawberries. Slice the lemon into rounds and stripe the leaves off the rosemary sprig.
Add all ingredients to a pitcher. Let sit in the refrigerator for 2 hours. Remove lemon slices and let sit for 2 more hours.
Strain out strawberries and rosemary with a fine strainer and store in the refrigerator for about 3 days.
hints: You may add extra strawberries and the lemon to each serving as garnish if desired.
You may leave out the stevia packet if desired.
If needed, adjust the serving size based on your personal fluid limitations or goals.

title: Pierogi with Sweet Cabbage and Mushroom Filling
description: Here’s a modernized kidney-friendly recipe for you to try in your household — Pierogi with Sweet Cabbage and Mushroom Filling — thanks to DaVita renal dietitian Christine from Illinois.
steps: Finely shred cabbage, finely chop onion and slice mushrooms.
Place flour in a bowl and make a well in the middle. Add egg, melted margarine and hot water.
Blend with a pastry knife until a dough forms. Turn onto a board and knead dough until smooth. Roll into a ball, cover and set aside for an hour.
Put cabbage in a medium saucepan, cover with water, and bring to a boil. Reduce heat and simmer for 15 to 20 minutes until tender. Drain cabbage and squeeze out extra liquid.
Sauté chopped onions and mushrooms in a tablespoon of oil until slightly caramelized.
Combine cabbage with onion and mushrooms. Set aside to cool.
After cooled, finely chop the vegetable mixture. Add pepper to taste and stir.
Roll out dough into a 10” to 11” circle. Cut 12 circles in the dough with a round cookie cutter.
Place a heaping teaspoon of filling in the middle of each dough circle. Fold over, stretch and press sides together to form a crescent-shaped dumpling.
Drop dumplings, two or three at a time, into a pot of boiling water. Pierogi will float to the top when done. Remove with a slotted spoon.
Once boiled, lightly fry dumplings in oil for a crispy treat, if desired.
hints: Adjust the hot water for proper consistency of dough. Dough should be smooth and pliable but not sticky.
To save time, you can use pre-shredded coleslaw cabbage.
The filling can be prepared ahead and refrigerated overnight, if needed.
This recipe yields 3 servings, but can easily be increased and extra uncooked pierogi frozen for later.
Garnish with a drizzle of melted margarine and a dollop of sour cream.

title: Grilled Chicken, Asparagus and Corn
description: Grilled Chicken, Asparagus and Corn is a chef-inspired recipe by Chef Frank Bonanno. Chef Bonanno and DaVita partnered to create kidney-friendly recipes for the DaVita Eats: Chef Tips video series.
serving_size: 3-1/2 ounces chicken, 1/2 ear of corn, 5 asparagus spears
ingredients: 8 ounces boneless, skinless chicken breast (1 large or 2 medium breasts)
1/2 teaspoon herb-spice mix (cumin, paprika, chili powder)
1 ear fresh corn on the cob (Colorado corn if available)
steps: Season chicken breast with one tablespoon olive oil, cracked black pepper, herb-spice mix and crushed red pepper flakes. Add chicken to hot spot of the grill, seasoned side down. Grill for 12 minutes.
While chicken cooks, cut asparagus and place on the grill. Season with black pepper and drizzle with 2 teaspoons of olive oil. Grill asparagus for 5 to 7 minutes.

Cut the ear of corn in half and drizzle with 1 teaspoon of olive oil. Grill corn for 3 to 4 minutes, until slightly charred. After taking corn off the grill, add a squeeze of lemon juice and the chopped chives.
Squeeze lemon over chicken and asparagus to taste.
hints: Fresh lemon juice and a little splash of olive oil is a great substitute for salt.
After asparagus starts to char, you can push it off to a part of the grill that isn’t in direct flame.
Cook an extra ear of corn for lunch or dinner tomorrow.
Adjust chicken portion to match your meal plan.
This recipe is featured in the DaVita Eats: Chef Tips video series.

title: Pasta Salad
description: Loaded with nutrient rich veggies, this dish gets its flavors from garlic and onion, as well as Mrs. Dash®, which is entirely salt- and MSG-free. The kidney-friendly Pasta Salad also calls for parmesan cheese, which has such a strong and unique flavor, a little goes a long way.
ingredients: 1 teaspoon Mrs. Dash® herb seasoning blend
steps: Finely mince onion, shred carrots, cut broccoli florets into small pieces, dice cucumber and chop bell pepper.
Combine vinegar, oil, garlic powder, pepper, oregano, celery seed and onion to make dressing. Set aside.
Cook pasta al dente; do not overcook.
Drain and rinse pasta. Toss with enough dressing to coat.
Add parmesan cheese to pasta and refrigerate for at least 12 hours.
Two hours before serving, add the remaining vegetables, Mrs. Dash® and paprika, and toss. Add more dressing if needed or desired.
Refrigerate until ready to serve.
hints: It’s important to refrigerate the Pasta Salad for a minimum of 12 (but no more than 24) hours before serving to allow the seasonings time to infuse into the pasta.
The amount of dressing and paprika used in this recipe is a matter of personal preference. Analysis includes all the dressing.

title: Zesty Chicken Wings
description: Some occasions seem to call for chicken wings, from sports events to family TV viewing, and so DaVita renal dietitian Lisa from Massachusetts made it her goal to create a kidney-friendly recipe that would have all tasters giving her Zesty Chicken Wings thumbs up.
steps: Chop green onions.
Mix all ingredients except the chicken wings. Set aside 3/4 cup of marinade.
Place chicken wings into a container, or large re-sealable plastic bag. Pour the extra marinade over wings.
Cover and marinate in the refrigerator 4 to 6 hours.
Preheat oven to 350° F.
Place chicken wings on a baking sheet, and bake for 20 minutes.
Meanwhile, in a small sauce pan, bring reserved 3/4 cup marinade to a boil. Reduce by 1/3 until it thickens slightly to a glaze (approximately 10 minutes).
After 20 minutes remove chicken from the oven, and brush wings with the glaze.
Raise oven temperature to 400° F and cook chicken wings about another 20 minutes, until done.
hints: Seven pounds whole chicken wings yields about 36 wings.
Chicken wing drummettes or boneless chicken pieces may be substituted for whole chicken wings. Adjust cooking time to avoid overcooking.

title: Mint Jelly Cream Cheese Dip
description: Green mint jelly is the secret to making a simple, 3 ingredient kidney-friendly appetizer.
steps: Open cream cheese and place entire bar onto a serving plate.
Spread jelly on the top of the cream cheese.
Serve with low-sodium crackers or flat bread.
hints: Prepare the night before or right before serving. It’s very easy and inexpensive!
You can use any jelly flavor, but green is nice for St. Patty’s Day. Try jalapeño pepper jelly for an extra kick.

title: Pineapple-Lime Freeze
description: Pineapple-Lime Freeze is an icy and refreshing treat fits into diabetes, dialysis and CKD non-dialysis diets. Low in calories, sodium, potassium and phosphorus, it’s also fat- and cholesterol-free. For added nutrition, you can mix protein powder into the lime juice before adding to the processed pineapple.
steps: Open the can of pineapple and drain.
Place pineapple chunks on a baking sheet in a single layer and freeze.
When chunks are frozen, place in food processor or blender.
Add limeade and lime juice. Process until well blended and fluffy in texture.
Serve immediately or freeze in 1/2-cup servings.
hints: Protein powder can be added for a more nutritious snack/dessert. Mix it into the lime juice before adding to the processed pineapple.
You can substitute 16 ounces frozen pineapple chunks for the canned pineapple and skip steps 1 and 2.

title: Poor Man’s Cake
description: Suitable for CKD and dialysis food plans, the cake calls for just a half cup of cocoa to give it a rich color and chocolaty taste. Kathy says that Michelle gave her the recipe because she wanted to help patients maintain good phosphorus control while enjoying their chocolate.
steps: Preheat oven to 350°F.
Mix the first 5 ingredients in an ungreased 9” x 13” baking pan.
Make 3 holes in the dry ingredients.
Pour 2 tablespoons vinegar in one hole.
Pour 3/4 cup oil in second hole.
Pour 2 teaspoons vanilla in the third hole.
Add 2 cups of cold water and mix.
Bake for 30 to 45 minutes until a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean.
hints: Great for cupcakes too! Pour 1/3 cup batter into each regular size cupcake liner to make 24 cupcakes.
Cocoa processed with alkali, also known as Dutch chocolate, is much higher in potassium than natural cocoa powder.

title: Ground Sirloin Pasties
description: DaVita renal dietitian, Shelli from Michigan, shares her kidney-friendly recipe for Ground Sirloin Pasties. Delicious pasties were introduced in the U.S. by Cornish miners, who immigrated to the Michigan Upper Peninsula in the 1800s. Shelli’s Ground Sirloin Pasties, also known as Upper Peninsula Pastie is a piecrust filled with hearty ingredients sirloin, vegetables and seasonings.
ingredients: 15-ounce package (2 crusts) rolled, refrigerated, unbaked pie crust
steps: Preheat oven to 375° F. Let pie crust stand at room temperature according to package directions.
Dice carrot and chop onion.
Brown ground sirloin in a large skillet over medium heat. Drain and set aside.
Place carrot in a microwave dish. Add 1 tablespoon water; cover and cook on high for 2 minutes. Add frozen corn, and peas; microwave for 2 minutes. Drain.
To make filling, combine meat, vegetables, onion, Worcestershire sauce, black pepper and thyme in a bowl.
On a lightly floured surface, unroll pie crusts. Cut each pie crust into four pieces.
Spoon 1/4 cup of the filling onto half of each piece of piecrust. Lightly moisten pie crust edges with a small amount of milk or egg white.
Fold other half of pie crust over filling. Seal edges by crimping with a fork. Cut slits in the top of the pastries. Brush top with egg white. Place on a large, ungreased baking sheet.
Bake for 15 to 20 minutes or until crust is golden brown. Cool slightly on wire racks.
Serve each pastie with 1 teaspoon ketchup.
hints: Wrap and freeze extra pasties for a quick meal later. Reheat in the oven or microwave.
For variety substitute ground turkey or chicken for beef.

title: Tzatziki Sauce
description: A traditional Greek sauce, Tzatziki Sauce is a refreshing addition to any burger or sandwich.
steps: Peel the cucumber then grate using the large holes of a box grater.
Remove some of the liquid from grated cucumber by lightly squeezing while holding over the sink.
In a small bowl mix cucumber with the Greek yogurt, garlic powder, dill, pepper and lemon juice to make tzatziki sauce.
Cover and place in the refrigerator until ready to serve.
hints: Serve Tzatziki Sauce with Turkey Meatball Gyros and Chickpea Burgers.

title: High Protein Rice Milk
description: Give your favorite rice beverage a protein boost to help meet the higher protein requirements of the dialysis diet.
steps: Combine rice milk and protein powder in a blender and blend well.
Divide into 2 servings. Enjoy one now and one later.
hints: Refrigerate extra serving until ready to drink.
EAS 100% Whey Protein Powder® was used in this recipe analysis. Ask your dietitian about other protein powder options.
Stir in a glass or shake in a shaker instead of the blender if desired.

title: Kotlet (Meat and Potato Patties)
description: For a kidney-friendly treat, follow us to the Middle East and sample some Kotlets, or meat and potato patties Persian style. This savory recipe was adapted for people following the renal diet by Zohreh, a Davita dietitian from California.
ingredients: 1 teaspoon Mrs. Dash® Original herb seasoning blend
steps: Peel and grate the potato, then soak in warm water for 2 hours to reduce potassium. Rinse, drain and squeeze excess water using a clean dish towel.
Grate the white onion; dice the red onion and shred the lettuce.
Mix ground beef, white onion, grated potato, egg, turmeric, garlic powder, black pepper and Mrs. Dash seasoning until well mixed.
Heat the oil in a medium-size skillet.
Make 5 patties (round, the size of your palm) and fry over medium heat until browned on both sides.
Serve each patty on a pita with lettuce, red onion and fresh basil.
hints: French bread, lavash, hamburger buns or tortillas are also good bread choices.
Use less oil and a non-stick pan to lower calorie and fat.
It’s easy to get very creative with Kotlets by adding or substituting various ingredients. Serve cold or hot for lunch, dinner or as an appetizer.
Shredded hash brown potatoes can be substituted for fresh potato. No need to soak potatoes if you are not on a potassium restriction.

title: Spiced Eggnog
description: For the holidays, try something a little different like the kidney-friendly recipe for Spiced Eggnog.
steps: Combine the half & half creamer, egg product, sugar, rum extract and pumpkin pie spice in a chilled blender and blend for 1 to 2 minutes.
Pour into 6 small glasses. Top each serving with a tablespoon of whipped topping and a sprinkle of nutmeg.
hints: Rum extract may be replaced with 2 tablespoons rum, if desired. Always check with your doctor before including alcohol in your diet.
Replace sugar with low-calorie sweetener to decrease carbohydrate to 4 grams and calories to 125 per serving.
Check half & half ingredients and avoid brands with phosphate additives.

title: Chicken and Watercress with Gratin Pasta
description: Chicken and Watercress with Gratin Pasta is a tasty one-dish kidney-friendly meal that provides a protein source with pasta and veggies.
steps: Cook the pasta according to package instructions, omitting salt.

Meanwhile, chop the onion, garlic cloves and watercress. Heat the oil in a skillet and sauté the onion and garlic. Add the shredded chicken and watercress. Mix well and cook until the watercress is wilted.
Once the pasta is cooked, drain and add the chicken mixture and half the béchamel sauce. Mix well.
Place the mixture into a baking dish sprayed with cooking spray. Cover with the remaining béchamel sauce. Sprinkle with the Parmesan cheese and bake 30 to 40 minutes until golden brown.
hints: Béchamel sauce is a basic white sauce.

title: Cloud Bread
description: Eggs and whey protein powder make Cloud Bread a good source of protein for dialysis patients who need a protein boost.
steps: Preheat oven to 300˚ F. Separate the eggs, setting aside the yolks for later.
With a stand or hand mixer whip the egg whites and cream of tartar until stiff peaks are formed. Set aside.
Mix the egg yolks in a bowl with the remaining ingredients and stir well to combine.
Using a small amount of egg whites gently fold into the yolk mixture a little at a time until it is well mixed. Continue to add remaining egg whites.
Pour the mixture into a greased loaf pan.
Bake in the center of the oven for 50 to 60 minutes, until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean.
Allow the cloud bread to cool. Remove from the pan and slice. Store in the refrigerator.
hints: Look for a brand of protein powder that has the lowest amount of phosphorus and potassium. Your renal dietitian may give you tips on brands available in your area.
This recipe used vanilla protein powder. Use other flavors or unflavored protein powder as desired.
For a savory flavor add garlic powder, onion powder or both.

title: Bow-Tie Pasta Salad
description: Bow-Tie Pasta Salad is a great recipe for the dialysis diet.
steps: Chop celery, and bell pepper. Shred carrots. Finely chop onion.
Mix pasta, celery, red bell pepper, carrot and onion in a bowl.
In a separate small bowl, blend pepper, mayonnaise, sugar and lemon juice until smooth.
Pour dressing mixture over pasta and vegetables and mix until well coated.
Chill and serve.
hints: Add fresh basil, tarragon or rosemary if desired.

title: Asian-Style Turkey Bowls
description: Asian-Style Turkey Bowls is a complete meal recipe featuring low potassium veggies, ground turkey, cilantro, Sriracha, ginger and coconut aminos instead of higher sodium soy sauce.
serving_size: 1-3/4 cups turkey and vegetables + 1/2 cup rice
ingredients: 1 tablespoon Mrs. Dash garlic and herb seasoning blend
steps: Prepare rice according to package instructions. Set frozen broccoli out to thaw. Dice the onion; slice celery; slice bell pepper into strips; mince garlic cloves, grate ginger and chop cilantro.
Drizzle canola oil in a large non-stick pan and heat to medium high heat. Add turkey and brown. Halfway through cooking add the Mrs. Dash herb seasoning. Once turkey is cooked, remove from pan.
In the same pan, add in onion, peppers and celery and cook over medium heat for 5 minutes. Add in garlic and ginger and cook for 3 more minutes.
Once vegetables are soft, add in frozen broccoli and stir to combine for a few more minutes.
To make the sauce, combine broth, brown sugar, coconut aminos and Sriracha sauce in a small bowl.
Add cooked turkey back into pan and stir in sauce to combine.
Place 1/2 cup rice in a bowl and top with turkey and vegetable mixture. Add chopped cilantro if desired. Enjoy!
hints: To thicken the sauce up more, add 1 teaspoon of corn starch.
If Mrs. Dash seasoning is unavailable you can combine 1/2 teaspoon pepper, 1 teaspoon onion powder and 1 teaspoon garlic powder.
Ginger paste can be substituted for fresh ginger.
For a lower protein diet, if you have CKD and are not on dialysis, decrease the ground turkey to 1/2 pound. Protein is decreased to 16 grams.

title: Cottage Cheese Sour Cream Pancakes
description: DaVita dialysis patient Gloria shares her recipe for Cottage Cheese Sour Cream Pancakes, a high protein, low phosphorus pancake treat.
steps: Beat eggs slightly. Add cottage cheese, sour cream, and salt.
Mix until blended; will not be smooth.
Gradually fold in flour.
Drop by 1/4 cupfuls well apart into hot oiled pan or onto non-stick griddle.
Cook until dry and brown around edges. Flip and brown other side.
hints: Suggested toppings include jam, jelly or canned fruit. Top with extra sour cream if desired.

title: Homemade Tomato Salsa
description: Small amounts of tomato are acceptable on a low potassium diet. DaVita dietitian Matilde from Texas shows you how to include tomato. Try her Homemade Tomato Salsa recipe with only 103 mg of potassium per serving.
steps: Chop the onion, tomato, cilantro and jalapeno into small pieces. Combine in a bowl.
Juice the lime. Add the lime juice, olive oil, salt and pepper to the vegetable mixture.
Let the salsa marinade for 15 minutes or more.
Serve with low-sodium tortilla chips or use as a topping on fish, chicken, meat or salad.
hints: Use red, white or yellow onion in this recipe.
The firmer the tomato, the better for this recipe.
The jalapeno is optional, or you may use another hot pepper of your choice.
A lime will produce about 2 tablespoons of juice.
Kosher salt and fresh ground pepper give a better flavor, if they are available.
Use a food processor to chop the vegetables if desired.

title: Green Beans with Turnips
description: Here’s a great way to get your vegetables. This Southern kidney-friendly recipe for Green Beans with Turnips packs a lot of flavor. It’s easy to make, just boil and add the spices. Yum.
steps: Remove ends from the green beans and cut into 1-1/2″ pieces. Peel turnips and dice each one into 8 pieces. Mince the garlic cloves.
Place vegetables and garlic in a medium-size pot. Cover with 3 cups water and bring to a boil. Reduce to medium heat and cook uncovered for 15 minutes.
Remove pot from heat and drain water. Add butter, pepper and salt. Gently toss to mix seasonings with vegetables. Serve hot.
Remove to serving dish and sprinkle with paprika.
hints: Add a dash of hot sauce if you like spicy vegetables.

title: Sheet Pan Chicken with Green Beans and Potatoes
description: Chicken dinner just got easier. Try DaVita dietitian Jackie’s Sheet Pan Chicken with Green Beans and Potatoes. It’s easy and only one pan to clean up.
steps: Preheat oven to 400˚ F. Chop the potatoes into bite sized pieces. See helpful hints for instructions on potassium reduction if needed. Toss potatoes in 1 teaspoon olive oil.

Spray a 9 x13-inch sheet pan with cooking spray. Place the raw chicken strips down 1/3 of the pan. Place the potatoes down another 1/3 of the pan. Finally, lay the frozen green beans down the last 1/3 of the pan.
Melt the butter and drizzle over the entire pan of chicken, potatoes and green beans. Sprinkle Italian dressing dry mix over the entire pan.
Bake for 20 to 30 minutes. Check chicken for doneness after 20 minutes.
hints: Nutrient analysis based on leached potatoes. If not leached the potassium content is 766 mg per serving.

To reduce potassium in potatoes: Chop potatoes. Place in a large pan and cover completely with water. Bring to a boil, then drain. Refill water over the potatoes, to cover by 1-inch. Bring to a boil again and boil for 10 minutes. Drain and toss with 1 teaspoon olive oil before adding to the sheet pan.
Packages of raw chicken breast strips will vary in weight. Generally they will weigh between 14-16 ounces. There are 16 ounces in 1 pound.

There are about 2 tablespoons of dry Italian dressing mix in a 19 gram packet. Look for a dry mix with the lowest amount of sodium possible. Be cautious, using too much dry mix will increase the sodium content of the meal.
Save the remaining Italian dressing mix and use for a different recipe or mix with sour cream for a vegetable dip.

title: Creamy Alfredo Sauce
description: Make this creamy alfredo sauce for your dinner. DaVita’s recipes are delicious, kidney-friendly, and submitted by DaVita dietitians.
steps: Sauté garlic in butter.
Add remaining ingredients. Simmer until a smooth consistency is attained.
Weigh finished sauce and divide by 10 to determine serving size weight.
hints: Store extra portions in the freezer in 2 ounce portion cups.

title: Cauliflower with Garlic Sauce
description: DaVita renal dietitian, Diana, has a quick and easy Cauliflower with Garlic Sauce recipe that’s a hit. Garlic, honey and apple cider vinegar join together to create a taste sensation that turns renal-friendly cauliflower into a vegetable dish the whole family can enjoy.
steps: In a large saucepan with steamer rack, steam cauliflower over boiling water 8 to 10 minutes or until crisp-tender (cover with lid while steaming).
In a small saucepan, cook minced garlic in olive oil for 30 seconds then remove pan from heat.
Stir in honey, apple cider vinegar and chopped parsley. Return saucepan to heat until sauce is heated.
Transfer steamed cauliflower to a serving dish.
Pour sauce over hot cauliflower and toss to coat.
hints: This is a quick and easy way to add a nutritious vegetable to your meal.

title: Pavlova with Strawberries
description: Try this delicious kidney-friendly recipe for Pavlova with Strawberries by DaVita dietitian Brenda from Washington. She uses some of her favorite regional foods so you can create a delicious, dialysis-appropriate meal with splendid flavors from the Pacific Northwest.
steps: Preheat oven to 300º F. Set egg whites out to bring to room temperature. Slice the strawberries and set aside.
Beat egg whites with salt at high speed until soft peaks form. Add 2 cups of the sugar, 1 tablespoon at a time, beating well after each addition. Gently fold in vinegar and 1-1/2 teaspoons vanilla.
Smooth mixture into an 8” round, ungreased cookie sheet or pizza pan. Smooth top.
Bake for 45 minutes. Turn off oven and let shell set for 1 hour with oven door shut. Remove from oven and let cool completely.

For the whipped cream, place bowl and whisk in the freezer for 10-15 minutes. Put sugar, heavy whipping cream, and remaining 1 teaspoon vanilla into bowl and whip until stiff. (Can be done with a hand mixer, stand mixer, or by hand.)
Fill Pavlova shell with whipped topping and sliced berries on top.
hints: When beating egg whites, start on low to medium speed until half whipped. At this point add pinch of salt or cream of tartar and increase mixer to high speed. The result is whipped whites that are more stable and take less time to whip.
Not recommended for people with diabetes due to high carbohydrate content.

title: Raspberry Lime Vinaigrette
description: It’s no wonder this raspberry lime vinaigrette is a go-to favorite for renal dietitian Judy from Pennsylvania. Fresh raspberries along with raspberry vinegar and raspberry preserves add a sweet berry flavor that complements salad greens without adding extra sodium.
steps: Crush raspberries and chop tarragon.
Whisk together first 7 ingredients.
Slowly whisk in oil until well blended. Serve.
Store remaining dressing in a tightly sealed jar and refrigerator until ready to serve. Keeps for up to one week.
hints: Two fresh limes yield approximately 1/4 cup lime juice.
Drizzle 2 tablespoons dressing over salad greens topped with fresh raspberries.
Substitute low sugar preserves or fruit spread to reduce carbohydrate to 5 grams.
Substitute 1/4 teaspoon dried terragon if fresh is unavailable.
Grape seed oil is a great tasting substitute for canola oil.

title: Vegetable Cutlets
description: Vegetable Cutlets is a kidney-friendly recipe that bursts with flavor. You can also add Cilantro Chutney on top as a delicious garnish.
ingredients: 2 cups frozen French style green beans
steps: Thaw and chop green beans. Grate carrots, cabbage and cilantro.
Soaked bread slices in water and drained by squeezing between the palms of your hands.
In a medium pan cover cabbage and carrots with water and boil for 10 minutes. Add the chopped green beans and cook until completely done. Drain excess water and cool.
Add spices, flour, bread slices, cilantro and lime juice to vegetables and mix well.
Make 12 balls and flatten each into a patty the size of a small burger.
Heat a saucepan over medium heat. Add the oil and place patties in the saucepan, two or three at a time without crowding. Flip patties over when cooked, about 2-3 minutes on each side.
Serve hot.
hints: Serving suggestions: Serve on a bun with mayonnaise, lettuce and onion or serve without bread and top with Cilantro Chutney or your favorite dipping sauce.
Freeze or refrigerate leftover cutlets for a quick meal or snack later.

title: Pineapple Squash
description: This renal-friendly squash dish has a unique flair. The pineapple gives it a sweet side that can be served as a side to any meal.
ingredients: 1 tablespoon butter, cut into small pieces
steps: Cut squash and zucchini into 1 inch cubes, dice the green bell pepper. Place squash in a 3-1/2 or 4 quart slow cooker.
In a small bowl, mix the pineapple, green bell pepper, cinnamon, brown sugar and butter.
Spoon mixture over squash and mix well.
Cover and cook on low heat setting for 6-7 hours or until squash is tender. Stir gently to mix.
Serve immediately.
hints: Diabetics may use Splenda® brown sugar substitute in equal amounts.

title: Plain Egg Whites
description: Nothing plain about this Plain Egg Whites recipe. It’s a great protein substitution for people with diabetes who are on dialysis.
steps: Add pasteurized liquid egg whites to greased fry pan.
Cook on medium heat, cover or flip over.
hints: Season with your favorite low-sodium herb seasoning blend.
Use butter instead of oil for extra flavor.
Make a sandwich or wrap or eat as a meat replacement with vegetables and starch.

title: Vanilla Milk Alternative
description: While there are plenty milk substitutes available to buy, why not make your own low potassium, low phosphorus substitute?
ingredients: 6 scoops vanilla EAS® 100% whey protein powder
steps: Mix 1/4 to 1/2 of recipe at a time in a blender (depending on size of blender) for 20 seconds to blend the protein powder in well.
Serve cold and enjoy!
hints: Recipe makes about 1/2 gallon. Store remaining beverage in a covered pitcher.

EAS whey protein powder used in the nutrition analysis contains 26 grams protein for 2 scoops. If you use a different brand of whey protein adjust the amount to provide approximately 156 grams protein for the recipe. Ask your dietitian about other protein powder options.
Substitute strawberry or chocolate whey protein powder for a different flavor beverage.

title: Chicken Squares
description: This dialysis-friendly recipe for Chicken Squares was submitted by DaVita renal dietitian Lori from Pennsylvania, who happens to know a lot about taste and convenience.
ingredients: 3/4 pound chicken breasts, bone in, with skin
steps: Preheat oven to 350° F. Set cream cheese out to soften. Melt butter.
Cook, drain, and chop broccoli.
Boil chicken breasts until done; drain, remove skin and bones, and dice into pieces.
Mix together chicken, softened cream cheese, melted butter and broccoli.
Open crescent rolls and form a rectangle with 2 rolls. Pinch seam to seal and stretch rectangle.
Place 1/4th of chicken mixture in center; fold edges across to make a turnover. Press edges to seal.
Bake for 25 to 30 minutes or until rolls are browned.
hints: Take a look at Chicken Squares as they are baking in oven periodically to make sure they don’t get too brown.
This is a higher sodium entrée. To keep sodium in check, complete the meal with low-sodium items such as salad, low-sodium dressing and fruit.
The chicken bones and skin add extra flavor during cooking. Fourteen ounces of boneless, skinless chicken breasts may be substituted for bone-in breasts if desired.
Freeze or refrigerate broth from boiling the chicken for later use in a recipe that calls for low-sodium chicken broth.
If fat-free cream cheese is substituted, fat is reduced to 16 grams and sodium is 577 mg.

title: Low-Sodium Albacore Tuna Salad
description: Thousand Island dressing and yellow mustard are the surprise ingredients in this tasty Low-Sodium Albacore Tuna Salad recipe.
ingredients: 2-2/3 ounces albacore white tuna, low-sodium, water packed
steps: Finely chop the celery and onion.
In a small bowl mix all ingredients together.
Weigh the finished salad and divide by 2 to determine weight of serving size.
hints: Virgil prefers StarKist® Low Sodium Albacore White Tuna because the sodium content is low. Check at Target if you are unable to find it at your local grocery store.

title: Slow Cooker Jellied Carrots
description: Try this easy and kidney-friendly recipe for Slow Cooker Jellied Carrots.
ingredients: 1 teaspoon Mrs. Dash® herb seasoning blend
steps: To prepare the carrots, peel, slice in half long ways, and cut each half into 4 pieces. Place in the slow cooker.
Add vinaigrette dressing, jelly, black pepper and herb seasoning. Stir to coat carrots.
Set slow cooker on low heat, cover with a lid and cook 3 to 4 hours until carrots are tender.
hints: Substitute frozen carrots or whole baby carrots instead of regular size raw carrots. No cutting required.

title: Pan-smoked Chicken Breast
description: Pan-smoked Chicken Breast uses a home-made kitchen smoker pan to infuse delicious smoky flavor to spice rubbed chicken breasts. This low-sodium dish is full of flavor.
steps: Combined the spices to make a rub mix.
Rinse the chicken breasts, pat dry, and brush lightly with oil.
Rub the chicken breasts with spice rub mix.
Refrigerate the chicken breast for 3 to 4 hours.
Preheat oven to 400º F.

To set up a smoke-roasting pan, place hardwood chips in a disposable foil pan and set a rack on top. Heat the pan over stovetop burner on medium-high until the smoke appears. Place the marinated chicken breasts on the rack and cover the pan tightly with foil.
Reduce heat to medium and smoke the chicken breast for 10 minutes.
Transfer the chicken breasts to a baking pan and roast in the oven for 10 minutes.
hints: Serve with white rice and Stir-Fry Vegetables.
Select chicken breasts that weigh approximately 4 ounces each uncooked.
Adjust the portion to match your meal plan if you are on a lower or higher protein diet.

title: Asparagus and Cheese Crepe Rolls with Parsley
description: Serve kidney-friendly Asparagus and Cheese Crepe Rolls with Parsley for dinner, breakfast or brunch.
steps: Steam the asparagus for 6 to 8 minutes.
Puree cream cheese with parsley, lemon juice and spices, to make a green cream sauce. Season to taste. Set aside.
To make crepes combine the flour, water, egg, egg white and 2 tablespoons melted butter; whisk to make a smooth batter.

Melt 1/2 tablespoon butter in a pan (8 to 10-inch crepe or sauté pan). Add 1/3 cup crepe batter and turn pan to spread batter. Cook until bubbly and edges begin to brown. Turn and cook briefly on the other side. Cool on a plate. Repeat with remaining butter and batter to make 4 crepes.
Spread crepes with cream cheese filling. Distribute the asparagus spears evenly at end of each crepe and firmly roll up into rolls.
Wrap in foil and let cool in refrigerator for one hour. Cut chilled crepes into 3 to 4 pieces with a sharp knife before serving.
hints: For a higher protein entrée fill the crepe with shrimp instead of asparagus. Peeled shrimp, sauté in olive oil, let it cool down and curl up in the crepes.

title: Picnic Potato Salad
description: Picnic Potato Salad is a kidney-friendly dish that should make an appearance at all your picnics or outdoor gatherings. Dialysis patients need to leach or soak their potatoes to lower the potassium content.
ingredients: 3/4 cup reduced-fat mayonnaise with olive oil
steps: Boil eggs to hard-cooked stage.

To reduce potassium in potatoes, peel potatoes, cut into small pieces, cover with water and bring to a boil. Discard the water and add fresh water. (Skip this part if a low potassium diet is not required.) Boil potatoes until tender but still firm when punctured with a fork.
While potatoes are cooking, finely chop celery, onion and bell pepper. Peel and chop hard boiled eggs.
Drain potatoes and place in a bowl. Add vegetables and chopped eggs. Do not stir.
Mix salad dressing ingredients together; add to potatoes and toss gently.
Cover and chill until ready to serve.
hints: Dialysis patients on a low potassium diet need to double boil potatoes to lower the potassium content. Skip step #2 if you are not on a low potassium diet.
If regular mayonnaise is substituted for reduced-fat mayonnaise fat increases to 24 grams per serving. Make this change if you need extra calories.
Use green or yellow bell peppers if desired, or try jalapeno peppers for a spicy flavor.

title: Blueberry Peach Crisp
description: Blueberry Peach Crisp features yummy blueberries, which are renal-friendly and packed with antioxidants, along with tasty peaches all warm and soft nestled under sweet crumbles. So delicious your family will never guess it came from a dialysis cookbook.
steps: Preheat oven to 375° F.
Pit and slice peaches into 3/4″ slices.
Spray 12″ x 9″ baking dish with cooking spray. Arrange peach slices and blueberries in dish.
Sprinkle sugar and lemon juice over the fruit.
Mix the flour and brown sugar in a bowl. Using two knives or a pastry blender, cut the butter into the flour and sugar mixture until it is crumbly. Sprinkle crumbs over the fruit.
Bake at for 45 minutes or longer until the fruit is soft and crumbs are browned.
Serve warm or at room temperature.
hints: Assemble crisp and place in oven right before dinner for a hot fruity dessert. Add a spoonful of whipped topping if desired.
Substitute 4 cups drained canned peach slices when fresh peaches are out of season.

title: Autumn Orzo Salad
description: Celebrate the fall season with Autumn Orzo Salad, an easy 4-step recipe to make ahead. It’s low in sodium, potassium and phosphorus–a great fit for a kidney diet.
steps: Cook orzo according to package instructions, omitting salt.
Core and dice apple. Chop basil.
In a medium bowl, add all the ingredients except the almonds. Combine until well incorporated.
Transfer the mixture to a serving dish and chill in the refrigerator for 30 minutes. Sprinkle with the almonds before serving.
hints: Three-fourths cup orzo makes 2 cups when cooked.
Fuji, gala and red delicious apples taste great in this salad.

title: Baked or Grilled Trout
description: North Carolina is known for their rainbow trout, so DaVita dietitian Barb has provided two healthy and kidney-friendly recipes for Baked and Grilled Trout.
steps: (Baked)
Preheat oven to 350° F.
Wash and dry fillets. Rub lightly with oil.
On a large sheet pan, place the fillets skin down.
Combine seasonings in a small bowl. Sprinkle evenly over fillets.
Bake uncovered for 10 to 15 minutes or until the trout fillets flake easily with a fork.
(Grilled)
Preheat grill on high heat.
Spray or brush fillet side of the trout fillets lightly with oil. Combine seasonings in a small bowl. Sprinkle evenly over fillets.
Place trout directly on the grill, fillet side down. Cook for 4 minutes. Spray or brush skin lightly with oil. Turn fillets over and cook until fish flakes easily with fork, about 3 to 5 minutes.
hints: For additional seasoning, try adding cayenne pepper.
If you are on a low-protein diet, adjust the serving size to your individual meal plan.

title: Chocolate Peanut Butter Muffins
description: If you’re a peanut butter and chocolate lover try this yummy combination in a flourless muffin created by DaVita renal dietitian Alissa from Nebraska.
steps: Preheat the oven to 350° F. Line a muffin tin with paper liners.
Melt butter and honey together. Whisk in cocoa powder and peanut butter until smooth.
Whisk in eggs and baking soda. Mix in chocolate chips. Pour evenly into muffin tin.
Bake for 18-22 minutes or until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean.
hints: If desired use almond butter in place of peanut butter. Almond butter has 24 mg more phosphorus and 16 mg more potassium per serving than peanut butter.
If preferred use reduced-fat peanut butter. This change will add approximately 4 grams of carbohydrate per serving.

Chocolate and peanut butter are high in potassium and phosphorus. The secret to including in a kidney diet is the portion–1 small muffin. Ask your dietitian if you need a phosphate binder with this muffin.

title: Renal-safe Macaroni and Cheese
description: Renal-safe Macaroni and Cheese is the kidney-friendly way to get your mac and cheese fix.
ingredients: 1 jar Kraft® Pimento Cheese spread made with cream cheese, 5-ounces
4 ounces canned Ortega® diced green chilies
steps: Rinse and drain green chilies.
Cook noodles in boiling water without salt or butter until the noodles are al dente.
Drain noodles. While noodles are hot, add the pimento cheese spread and chilies.
Stir until the cheese spread is melted into the noodles.
Serve hot. Add pepper at the table for taste, if desired.
hints: Elbow, shell or bowtie pasta are great choices for this recipe.
For a higher protein variation, add browned and drained ground beef.

Most cheese spreads are very high in sodium and phosphorus. The pimento spread in this recipe is made with cream cheese instead of processed cheese. (Look for the Philadelphia® brand cream cheese logo on the label). This is what keeps the sodium and phosphorus content low enough for a renal diet. Avoid bottled or canned spreads made with processed cheese.

title: Quick Microwaved Cinnamon Apples
description: Expand your culinary repertoire with a new idea for a dessert. DaVita dietitian, Lynn from Maryland, says you can make any meal better with her kidney-friendly recipe for Quick Microwave Cinnamon Apples.
steps: Wash and core apples. Trim 1-2 inches of the peel from the top of the apples.
Place apples in a high-sided microwave-safe bowl.
Pour honey into center of cored apples.
Add nutmeg and cinnamon.
Cover bowl with a microwave-safe lid. Microwave on high for about 6 minutes.
Serve immediately, topped with whipped topping.
hints: Small microwave ovens require 6 minutes to cook a medium apple. Cooking times vary depending on the size of the apples and the microwave. Apple is done when it is easy to cut.
Avoid covering food with plastic wrap during microwaving due to possible contamination of food with toxins from the plastic.
Reduce portion to 1/2 apple for a lower carbohydrate dessert.

title: Flank Steak
description: Flank Steak is a chef inspired recipe by Chef Frank Bonanno, owner of 11 Denver restaurants and host of "Chef Driven", a PBS series that showcases Colorado cuisine. Chef Bonanno and DaVita partnered to create kidney-friendly recipes and videos for the DaVita Eats: Chef Tips video series.
steps: Heat a sauté pan over high heat until hot.
Add olive oil to the pan.
Season the steak with black pepper and paprika.
Add the steak to the hot pan and sear over high heat for 4 minutes on each side.
Remove the steak from the pan and let it rest for 2 to 3 minutes.
Slice on the bias and serve.
hints: Let the steak rest before cutting it right away. This allows the flavors to settle in nicely.
Adjust portion to match your meal plan.
This recipe is featured in the DaVita Eats: Chef Tips video series.

title: Cran-Apple Cinnamon Snack Mix
description: A handful or two of snack mix can go a long way to satisfy cravings for a sweet and savory crunchy snack. DaVita dietitian Mary shared her kidney-friendly recipe for Cran-Apple Cinnamon Snack Mix.
steps: Preheat oven to 300° F. Spray a large rectangular cake pan (9″ x 13″ or larger) with non-stick cooking spray.
Dice the dried apples.
In a large bowl mix cereals and dried fruit; set aside.
In a medium bowl beat egg whites, sugar, apple juice and cinnamon with a whisk or hand mixer until foamy.
Pour egg mixture over cereal in bowl, stirring until evenly coated.
Sprinkle with sesame seeds.
Spread mixture into baking pan and bake for 45 minutes, stirring every 15 minutes, until cereal is lightly brown and crispy.
Cool completely. Store in an airtight container.
hints: Mary uses All Whites® pasteurized liquid egg white product. You can substitute 1/4 cup fresh egg whites.
Replace sugar with preferred low carbohydrate sweetener to reduce carbohydrate to 38 grams per serving. If you have diabetes consider adjusting the portion to 1/2 cup in addition to this change.

title: Arroz con Gandules (Rice with Pigeon Peas)
description: Arroz con Gandules is a tasty and kidney-friendly rice dish that is healthy and festively colorful — a perfect meal for family or to serve at a dinner party.
steps: Drain and rinse pigeon peas. Mince garlic.
Heat 2 teaspoons oil in a large saucepan.
Add Sofrito, Bijol® powder, tomato paste, garlic, oregano, bouillon cube and pigeon peas.
Stir fry for approximately 3 to 4 minutes to seal in juices.
In large sauce pan, prepare rice following the recipe on the package, omitting salt.
Mix rice in with the ingredients in large saucepan and serve.
hints: See Sofrito recipe on DaVita.com.
For more protein add one-cup chopped chicken. Adds 4 grams of protein per serving. Use half a rotisserie chicken with the skin and bones removed to save time.
Bijol®, a brand name for achiote or annotto powder, gives a yellow-orange color to the rice. It is a replacement for saffron. If unavailable, substitute equal parts paprika and turmeric.
Frozen or dried cooked pigeon peas may be substituted for canned peas.

title: Rice Pilaf
description: DaVita renal dietitian, Mary Anne from California, shares her Rice Pilaf recipe. This kidney-friendly side dish is much lower in sodium than a store-bought mix because you make it yourself at home.
ingredients: 1 cup vermicelli, broken into small pieces
steps: Chop onion, celery and parsley. Break vermicelli into small pieces.
Melt margarine in a skillet that has a cover.
Sauté onion and celery for 1 minute.
Add the rice and vermicelli and stir for 30 seconds.
Add the chicken broth, water and parsley. Bring to boil.
Cover and reduce to simmer about 15 minutes until all the liquid is absorbed.
hints: Angel hair pasta can be substituted for the vermicelli in this recipe.

title: Mushroom and Red Pepper Omelet
description: If you’re looking for a breakfast that is filling and delicious, look to the kidney-friendly recipe, Mushroom & Red Pepper Omelet.
steps: Dice the mushrooms, onion and red peppers.

Melt 1 teaspoon of the butter in a skillet over medium heat. Add the mushrooms and onion; sauté 5 minutes until onion is tender. Stir in diced red pepper. Remove vegetables from skillet and set aside.

Melt the remaining teaspoon of butter in the skillet. Beat eggs with Worcestershire sauce and cook over medium heat. Cook the omelet evenly by shaking the pan and gently lifting edges to allow uncooked egg to run underneath cooked egg.
When eggs are partially cooked, top with vegetable mixture. Place dollops of whipped cream cheese over vegetables. Continue cooking until eggs are set.
Remove the skillet from heat and fold omelet in half. Sprinkle with pepper. Divide into two portions and serve.
hints: Sautéed onion will appear transparent but not brown when cooked.
Compare sodium content on bottled or canned red peppers.
Reduce fat and cholesterol by using nonstick cooking spray or a nonstick skillet, trans-fat free margarine instead of butter and liquid low cholesterol egg substitute instead of whole eggs.

title: Pasta with Cauliflower
description: Pasta with Cauliflower is a healthy, easy and kidney-friendly recipe to serve at your next gathering.
serving_size: 1 cup pasta with 1/2 cup cauliflower sauce
steps: Wash cauliflower and cut into bite-sized pieces. Finely chop onion and mince garlic.
Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add onion and garlic and sauté for about 5 minutes until onion is transparent.
Add cauliflower, black and red pepper and sauté for 5 minutes.
Add chicken broth and bring to a boil. Reduce heat to simmer and allow cauliflower to cook until tender.

Cook linguine according to package directions, omitting salt. Drain and return to the pot used to cook it. Add several spoonfuls of the broth from cauliflower mixture to linguine and toss to prevent sticking.
Divide linguine into 8 individual servings and top with cauliflower and broth.
Add 1 tablespoon grated Parmesan cheese and more black and red pepper to taste. Chop parsley and garnish each serving evenly.
hints: Limit Parmesan cheese to 1 tablespoon per portion to keep phosphorus low.

title: Mexican Seasoning
description: Mexican Seasoning is a kidney-friendly recipe that can be put on beef, chicken or seafood.
steps: Mix spices together in a small jar or bowl.
Store in a jar or covered container for up to 6 months.
Use to season meat or vegetables for tacos, fajitas or burritos.
hints: Use as a dry rub, add to sour cream or Greek yogurt to make dip or season your favorite homemade salad dressing.
Adjust cayenne pepper to suit your taste.

title: Caraway Cabbage and Rice
description: DaVita renal dietitian Sara from California shares Caraway Cabbage with Rice, a low-sodium, kidney-friendly recipe that’s crunchy, great-tasting and healthy too.
steps: Shred cabbage and chop onion.
Spray a nonstick frying pan with cooking spray and sauté the onion and cabbage until limp.
Add water, Worcestershire sauce and caraway seeds. Cook for 3 minutes. Stir to prevent burning.
Drain mandarin oranges and add to cabbage mixture. Stir in hot rice.
Remove from heat and serve.
hints: Use coleslaw mix instead of cabbage if desired.

title: Ranch Dressing
description: Try this kidney-friendly Ranch Dressing recipe and you will never buy the pre-made dressing again.
steps: Place all the ingredients in a jar with a lid. Shake well until ingredients are blended.
Refrigerate for 30 minutes before serving.
hints: Substitute with low-fat mayonnaise and sour cream to reduce fat and calories.

title: Soft Tacos with Mexican Seasoning
description: Many ethnic meals have become American meals, and people on a kidney diet also want to enjoy the unique flavors they have come to enjoy from other countries. Soft Tacos with Mexican Seasoning is a kidney-friendly recipe that lets kidney patients keep taco night on their weekly menu.
steps: Make the Mexican Seasoning recipe (under Sauces and Seasoning in the Recipe section of DaVita.com).
Chop the onion and lettuce.
Brown and drain the ground beef. Add the seasoning mixture and the low-sodium tomato sauce. Heat over medium heat. Warm the tortillas.
To assemble soft tacos, take 1 flour tortilla, add 1/4 cup seasoned ground beef, 1 teaspoon cheese, 1 teaspoon onion, 1 teaspoon sour cream and lettuce as desired.
hints: Ground turkey or vegetarian ground meat substitute can be used instead of ground beef.

title: Jambalaya
description: Tonight you can bring that New Orleans Creole-style flavor to your dinner table. DaVita dietitian Brittney shows you how to “spice things up” with her delicious kidney-friendly recipe for Jambalaya.
steps: Preheat oven to 350º F.
Chop onion, bell pepper and garlic. Peel shrimp.
In a large bowl combine all ingredients except margarine.
Pour into a 9” x 13” baking dish and spread out evenly.
Slice margarine and place over top of ingredients.
Cover with a lid or foil.
Bake for 1 hour and 15 minutes. Serve hot.
hints: Uncle Ben’s® converted white rice is a popular brand. Converted rice, also know as parboiled rice, is steamed before it is husked. As a result the kernals absorb nutrients from the husk and the rice cooks more quickly.
1 stick of butter or margarine is equal to 1/2 cup.
For variation, try substituting cooked cubed chicken for shrimp.

title: Strawberry Bread
description: DaVita renal dietitian, Gaye from Tennessee, tells us she bakes kidney-friendly recipe Strawberry Bread in a small aluminum pan, and then wraps it in cellophane and ribbon to make a creative, fun and, most of all, delicious gift.
ingredients: 2-1/2 cups fresh strawberries or 14 ounces no-sugar-added frozen strawberries
steps: Preheat oven to 350° F degrees.
Finely chop the strawberries.
In a medium mixing bowl, beat the eggs. Add the canola oil and strawberries and stir well.
Mix the dry ingredients together in a separate large mixing bowl.
Make a well in the center of the dry ingredients and pour in the egg mixture.
Use a large spoon and mix until well blended; do not over mix.
Pour the batter into two ungreased 9″ x 5″ loaf pans. Bake 50 to 60 minutes.
Cool for 15 minutes, then use a knife to loosen the sides of the bread from the loaf pans and remove gently. Finish cooling on a rack.
Serve or wrap the bread in plastic wrap or foil to keep it fresh. Loaves can be refrigerated or frozen.
hints: Check if loaves are cooked through by inserting a toothpick down into the center. If it comes out clean, the loaf is done.
Refrigeration keeps the berries fresher-tasting in the bread.

For people with diabetes, substitute Splenda® Sugar Blend for Baking for sugar and low cholesterol egg product for eggs. 1 slice equals 206 calories, 23 grams carbohydrate, 11 grams fat and 0 mg cholesterol.
2-1/2 cups chopped strawberries is approximately 14 ounces.

title: Pineapple Slaw
description: Enjoy fruit and vegetables in a delicious Pineapple Slaw by DaVita renal dietitian Barbara in Arizona. She keeps it simple, healthy and kidney-friendly with only four tasty ingredients.
ingredients: 20 ounces canned crushed pineapple in unsweetened juice
steps: Shred cabbage and carrots and combine in a 2 quart bowl.
Add crushed pineapple with juice and dried cranberries to bowl.
Mix slaw ingredients together and chill in refrigerator at least 30 minutes before serving.
hints: Shred cabbage into coleslaw size pieces using a food processor or chop with a sharp knife.
2-1/2 cups shredded cabbage is approximately 3/4 of a small head of cabbage.

title: Lettuce and Mushroom Salad
description: The next time you’re in the mood for a crisp salad, try the kidney-friendly recipe Lettuce and Mushroom Salad.
steps: Chop onion and shred carrot.
Combine vegetables in a large bowl and toss.
Divide into 4 portions and serve in chilled salad bowls.
hints: Use exact measures to ensure potassium content is not too high.
Add your favorite low-sodium salad dressing.

title: Sweet Popcorn Balls
description: Sweet Popcorn Balls are a mouthwatering treat that’s tasty any time of year. Enjoy this kidney-friendly recipe as an appetizing afternoon snack or as a delectable dessert. Sweet Popcorn Balls is bound to become a staple in your kidney diet.
steps: Pop popcorn and put in a large bowl. Set aside for use later.

Mix syrup, brown sugar, water and vinegar in a saucepan. Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly until mixture boils. Continue cooking and stirring almost constantly about 15-20 minutes on medium heat. Cook to hard ball stage (until a small amount of mixture forms a hard ball when tested in very cold water.)
Remove from heat, quickly add butter, and stir.
Slowly pour mixture over popped popcorn in a large bowl, while mixing well. Form into balls, using as little pressure as possible.
Wrap each popcorn ball in plastic wrap and store in an airtight container.
hints: Butter hands, or better yet, wear rubber gloves with butter on them. The popcorn won’t stick as bad and is not as hot!

title: White BBQ Sauce
description: White BBQ Sauce is tomato-free, which makes it low in potassium compared to traditional BBQ sauce. Experiment with this kidney-friendly sauce to find your favorite ways to add extra flavor.
steps: Combine all of the ingredients in a bowl and whisk together.
Refrigerator for 30 minute to let the flavor blend.
hints: Add White BBQ Sauce while grilling poultry, meat, or vegetables; use as a marinade or serve as a side sauce.
Substitute lower fat mayonnaise and omit the 1/8 teaspoon of salt if desired.

title: Grilled Salmon with Herb Crust
description: Like a true Texan, DaVita renal dietitian Elaine from Texas is adding some spice to her recipe for Grilled Salmon with Herb Crust. Oregano, cilantro, green onion, garlic, lemon juice and olive oil create a tasty herb crust whether preparing this salmon dish in the oven or on the grill.
steps: Preheat oven to 400° F or preheat grill.
Using aluminum foil, create 1 cooking pocket for each fillet (if using frozen salmon, make sure it’s fully thawed).
Chop oregano, cilantro, green onions and garlic. Combine with lemon juice, olive oil, salt and pepper in a food processor. Process to chop and mix.
Coat the salmon fillets generously with herb mixture.
Place each fillet in foil pocket and seal.
Place foil pockets on a baking sheet or grill plate if cooking on a grill.
Bake for 30 minutes or until done, or grill for 6 to 8 minutes depending on thickness.
hints: Use either fresh or frozen salmon. When using frozen salmon, make sure it is fully thawed before cooking.
Salmon can be baked in the oven or cooked on the grill.
Adjust portion size to meet your protein goals.

title: Garlic Chicken with Balsamic Vinegar
description: DaVita renal dietitians are always on the lookout for simple, gourmet-tasting dishes with great nutrition for their dialysis patients. Carrie from Texas found a winner when she discovered kidney-friendly Garlic Chicken with Balsamic Vinegar. Enjoy the hearty flavors of garlic and balsamic vinegar blending together to make the chicken taste like it came from your favorite restaurant.
steps: Wash and trim excess fat from chicken breasts.
Coat both sides of chicken breast with pepper.
Heat olive oil in nonstick skillet over medium-high heat, and cook until nicely browned on one side (about 3 minutes).
Add garlic, turn chicken and scatter mushrooms all over.
Move chicken and mushrooms around to keep them from sticking and cook about 3 minutes.
In a small bowl, mix balsamic vinegar, low-sodium chicken broth, bay leaf, thyme leaves and cornstarch.
Add mixture to skillet with chicken. Stir until sauce is thickened.
Cover and cook over moderately-low heat for about 10 minutes.
Remove bay leaf and garlic before serving. Serve over rice or pasta.
hints: If you are on a lower protein diet, try this recipe but reduce the portion to match your diet plan.
Refrigerate leftover chicken to use in a salad or sandwich the next day.

title: Island Shrimp Slaw
description: Eileen, DaVita renal dietitian from New York, shares a taste of the tropics with her kidney-friendly recipe for Island Shrimp Slaw recipe. It’s the perfect combination of crunchy, traditional slaw with savory, spicy shrimp.
ingredients: 12 ounces frozen cooked shrimp, peeled and de-veined
steps: Chop onion, bell peppers and cilantro.
Thaw shrimp and pat dry.
In a large bowl, mix shrimp, coleslaw mix, onion, pepper, cilantro and 1/8 teaspoon cayenne pepper.
In a small bowl combine mayonnaise, sour cream, lemon juice, Italian seasoning and remaining1/8 teaspoon cayenne pepper. Pour dressing over shrimp cabbage mixture and toss well.
Chill for 2 hours and serve.
hints: If all ingredients are chilled prior to preparation, the 2-hour chill time can be eliminated.
If you want to “kick it up a notch,” add more cayenne pepper to taste.
For variety and a touch of sweetness, add 1/2 cup pineapple tidbits.

title: Chicken with Apples, Carrots and Grains
description: If you’re looking for a way to add whole grains to your kidney diet, this is the recipe to try. DaVita dietitian Deanna from Michigan created Chicken with Apples, Carrots and Grains to share with her dialysis patients. It’s low in sodium, potassium and phosphorus and high in fiber and flavor.
ingredients: 1 packet of Seeds of Change® Quinoa and Brown Rice
steps: Peel, rinse, and dice the onion and carrots. Core and dice the apples.
In a small bowl, mix cinnamon, coriander, cumin and pepper.
Pat chicken dry with paper towels. Cut in cube shapes and rub pieces with spice mixture.

In a large skillet over medium-high-heat add 1 tablespoon of oil. Add the onion, carrots and apples. Cook, stirring occasionally until the vegetables start to brown, about 15 minutes. Transfer to a medium bowl.
Add the remaining tablespoon of oil to the skillet. Brown the chicken for 2 to 4 minutes per side. Add broth and packet of quinoa and brown rice. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 15 to 25 minutes.
Add the dried cranberries and vegetable/fruit mixture. Cook until liquid is almost gone, 5 to 10 minutes.
hints: Brown rice and quinoa are gluten-free. If you have Celiac disease this recipe is a good choice.
Brown rice and quinoa are a good source of fiber and whole grains.

title: Green Juice
description: Juicing is a heath trend that has taken off over the past few years. Green Juice was created with lower potassium fruits and vegetables to help those on a kidney diet stay within their meal plan goal for potassium.
steps: Wash all produce well.
Core the apples.
Process all ingredients through a juicer. Divide into 2 servings and enjoy!
hints: Consult with your dietitian when incorporating juicing into your kidney diet. Juice blends are high in potassium and may not be recommended if potassium control is an issue.
Be sure to count 3/4 cup (6 ounces) as 1 vegetable and 2 fruit servings from your daily goal to stay within your potassium goal for the day.

title: Deviled Green Beans
description: Add a flavor punch to your next meal with this kidney-friendly recipe for Deviled Green Beans. Yellow mustard, black pepper and Worcestershire sauce turn tame green beans into a devilishly delicious treat.
steps: Prepare green beans as directed on package.
Make a sauce by mixing together 2 teaspoons melted butter, mustard, pepper and Worcestershire sauce. Heat in microwave for 30 seconds.
Toss sauce with hot cooked green beans.
Mix remaining margarine (melted) with bread crumbs. Sprinkle on top of the beans and serve.
hints: Substitute fresh green beans for frozen when in season.

title: Honey-Maple Snack Mix
description: A DaVita dietitian shares a kidney-friendly snack that is both nutritious and delicious: Honey-Maple Snack Mix.
ingredients: 10 ounces Cinnamon Teddy Grahams® snack cookies
steps: Combine Golden Grahams, Rice Chex, Teddy Grahams and pretzels in a large bowl.
Melt butter in a small saucepan; add brown sugar, honey and maple syrup. Cook over low heat until sugar is melted.
Pour over cereal mixture and mix well until all pieces are coated.
Preheat oven to 325° F.

Prepare 3 jelly roll pans by lining with aluminum foil and spraying the foil with cooking spray. (Can be done in 3 batches). Spread cereal mixture evenly over pans. Bake at 325° F for 20 minutes; stirring once halfway though.
Mix cranberries and apple chips; divide evenly among pans and stir.
Bake 5 more minutes; cool completely and store in an airtight container.
hints: For an extra twist sprinkle trail mix with Mrs. Dash® Caribbean Citrus or Fiesta Lime seasoning blend.
If you have diabetes, reduce portion size to 1/2 cup for a lower carbohydrate snack.
Look in the produce section for apple chips if you do not find it in the snack section.
Share extra servings with family and friends or cut recipe in half to make less.

title: Glazed Carrots
description: Naturally sweet carrots can be dressed up with a little ginger, apple juice and a few other ingredients to create this tasty kidney-friendly recipe for Glazed Carrots. This quick, easy recipe dresses up an already delicious vegetable making it a special treat.
steps: Slice carrots into 1-inch thick slices. Place carrots and 1/4 cup water in a pot. Cover and cook until slightly tender.
Mix together sugar, cornstarch, salt, ginger, apple juice and melted butter. Pour mixture over carrots and water.
Cook, stirring occasionally, for 10 minutes or until mixture thickens.
hints: Fresh carrots are best but you can substitute frozen carrots.
If desired, replace ginger with ground cinnamon.

title: Zingy Spiced Pears
description: If it’s something different yet yummy you want for dessert, try the kidney-friendly recipe for Zingy Spiced Pears.
steps: Preheat oven to 350° F.
Arrange pear slices in an 11” x 7” x 2” baking dish.
Combine Splenda brown sugar blend, ginger, rum extract, cinnamon and allspice.
Sprinkle brown sugar mixture over pears.
Dot with margarine.
Bake for 20 minutes.
Serve hot or refrigerate at least 1 hour to serve chilled.
hints: Bartlett amd Bosc pears are the best varieties for baking.
